---
title: "Solution: Interactions and Transformations"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(broom)
```

```{r load-data}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
```

## Task 1: Fit the additive model

```{r task1}
mod_add <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut, data = diamonds)
summary(mod_add)
# One slope for log(carat), different intercepts per cut level.
```

## Task 2: Fit the interaction model

```{r task2}
mod_int <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) * cut, data = diamonds)
summary(mod_int)
# Each cut level gets its own intercept AND its own slope for log(carat).
# log(carat) * cut expands to: log(carat) + cut + log(carat):cutGood
#   + log(carat):cutVery Good + log(carat):cutPremium + log(carat):cutIdeal
```

## Task 3: AIC comparison

```{r task3}
AIC(mod_add, mod_int)

cat("ΔAIC:", round(AIC(mod_add) - AIC(mod_int), 1), "\n")
# The interaction model has lower AIC. A ΔAIC > 10 is strong evidence.
# Whether the improvement justifies the extra 4 parameters (one per
# interaction term) depends on the context and practical significance.
```

## Task 4: Prediction grid — are lines parallel?

```{r task4}
grid <- diamonds |>
  data_grid(
    carat = seq_range(carat, n = 10),
    cut
  ) |>
  gather_predictions(mod_add, mod_int) |>
  mutate(pred_price = exp(pred))

ggplot(grid, aes(x = carat, y = pred_price, colour = cut)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "RdYlGn") +
  labs(
    title    = "Predicted price: additive vs interaction model",
    subtitle = "Additive: parallel lines (same carat slope). Interaction: lines fan out.",
    x        = "Carat",
    y        = "Predicted price (USD)",
    colour   = "Cut"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# In mod_add the lines are exactly parallel — the slope of carat is
# identical across all cut levels. In mod_int the lines diverge —
# Ideal diamonds have a slightly different (and in fact somewhat lower)
# price elasticity for carat than Fair diamonds.
```

## Task 5: Interpret the interaction coefficient

```{r task5}
int_coef <- coef(mod_int)["log(carat):cutIdeal"]
cat("log(carat):cutIdeal coefficient:", round(int_coef, 4), "\n")

# Interpretation:
# The slope of log(carat) is ___ units different for Ideal-cut vs Fair-cut diamonds.
# A negative value means: for Ideal-cut diamonds, each 1% increase in carat
# is associated with a slightly smaller percentage increase in price than
# for Fair-cut diamonds. Ideal diamonds command a fixed quality premium
# (the intercept shift), but the marginal value of additional carat
# weight is slightly lower for them.
```

## Task 6: Polynomial model

```{r task6}
mod_poly <- lm(log(price) ~ poly(log(carat), 2) + cut, data = diamonds)
summary(mod_poly)

AIC(mod_add, mod_poly)

# The quadratic term (degree 2 polynomial) is typically significant
# (p < 0.05), indicating a slight non-linearity in the log-log relationship.
# However, AIC may favour mod_poly or mod_int over mod_add only slightly.
# The key finding: the log-log transformation already captures most of the
# non-linearity; the quadratic adds only modest improvement.
```
